label: US Congress
_comment_feeds: Media attention is the gate. An item only qualifies if it surfaced here first. Edit freely - feeds break, that is normal. Remove a dead one rather than debugging it.
_comment_scoring: Deterministic. The model never scores. Each rule is a plain fact read off the Congress.gov response.
_comment_cap: Hard ceiling. If only one item clears the threshold the episode has one item. If none clear it, the episode says so and the sphere yields its slot.
_comment_script: Rules handed to the model verbatim when it writes the podcast script.
scriptRules: The listener has already read today's news. Never recap what happened. Start from what the coverage did not have room for.
Every factual claim must come from the supplied documents or article text. If something is not in the material, say that it is not in the material.
Mark provenance out loud: what the bill text states, what a sponsor claims, and what is contested are three different things and must sound different.

The listener is Swedish and follows US politics as an interested outsider, not a specialist. Never use a procedural term (markup, cloture, reconciliation, discharge petition) without explaining it in the same sentence.
Always answer why it matters, not only what moved.
Write in Swedish, for the ear. Spoken sentences, no headings, no bullet points, no stage directions.
